about.label: About
about.heading: About Me
about.text: My professional journey began in Production Planning and Control (PPC), where I developed a practical understanding of manufacturing operations, resource management, and the importance of reliable information in business decision-making.
about.detail: This experience led me into enterprise resource planning systems, where I have built a 16-year career, including 8 years focused on ERP consulting and implementation, specializing in TOTVS Protheus.
about.paragraph3: Throughout my career, I have worked across manufacturing, commercial, and retail environments, contributing to ERP implementations, system configuration, application support, requirements analysis, and process improvement. My approach combines business process knowledge with the technical ability to translate operational needs into effective solutions.
about.paragraph4: Alongside my functional expertise, I have developed strong technical skills in ADVPL/TLPP, SQL Server, Python, and systems integration, building customizations, automation tools, and solutions that improve operational efficiency and support the evolution of enterprise systems.
about.paragraph5: I believe technology delivers its greatest value when it connects people, processes, and information. This perspective guides my work: understanding business needs, identifying opportunities, and developing solutions that deliver meaningful results.

fiscal.title: Fiscal Classification Automation
fiscal.description: Development of a TOTVS Protheus solution to automate invoice tax classification, validate tax rules, and handle discrepancies, reducing manual intervention in the process.
fiscal.overview1: A project to automate the tax classification of invoices for John Deere parts in TOTVS Protheus ERP, developed collaboratively by the internal team and an external consultancy.
fiscal.overview2: The initiative aimed to reduce manual activities, standardize tax rules, and improve the efficiency of incoming fiscal document processing.
fiscal.challenge1: The process relied on manual intervention by the Tax team after the physical inspection of goods.
fiscal.challenge2: Items had to be analyzed, fiscal operations determined, taxes checked, and invoices classified, creating risks of rework and delays.
fiscal.solution1: Implementation of automation integrated with TOTVS Protheus through the OA060DOK entry point, identifying eligible suppliers, applying configured tax rules, and using intelligent TES.
fiscal.solution2: The solution validates taxes in the XML against amounts calculated by the ERP, including ICMS, IPI, PIS, and COFINS.
fiscal.solution3: Invoices that pass validation can proceed to automatic classification. Documents with discrepancies remain pending for manual review, with notification to the Tax team.
fiscal.role2: Given the scope of the work, the complexity of tax rules, and the high expectations for results, the project was developed in partnership with an external consultancy, using a technical collaboration model in which both parties actively participated in developing the solution.
fiscal.role3: My role included requirements analysis, defining and assessing technical alternatives, working directly with the consultancy's developers to implement business rules in Protheus, analyzing functionality, identifying and fixing issues, and implementing improvements throughout development.
fiscal.role4: The project involved the Tax team, responsible for defining and validating tax rules, and Project Management, responsible for coordinating the work.

fiscal.skill3: Collaborative development with an external consultancy.

userAutomation.title: User Registration Automation
userAutomation.description: Automation developed with Python and Playwright to register approximately 140 users in TOTVS Protheus, supporting the operational integration of six new business units.
userAutomation.overview1: During the integration of six new business units, approximately 140 users needed to be registered in TOTVS Protheus ERP within a short timeframe.
userAutomation.overview2: To meet this need, automation was developed using Python and Playwright to perform registration operations through the Protheus WebApp interface.
userAutomation.overview3: This approach made it possible to use features already available in the ERP and reduce repetitive registration work.
userAutomation.challenge1: The number of users and the available timeframe made manual registration an operationally demanding task.
userAutomation.challenge2: The Protheus WebApp interface also had specific behaviors, including dynamic elements, fields requiring particular interactions, and windows that appeared only after the correct sequence of actions.
userAutomation.challenge3: The automation also had to use information from a CSV file prepared by third parties, making input data quality an important dependency.
userAutomation.solution1: Automation was developed in Python using Playwright to interact with the TOTVS Protheus WebApp interface.
userAutomation.solution2: The solution used a CSV file as its record source and performed registration through existing ERP features, including the use of template users as a reference for new registrations.
userAutomation.solution3: During development, interface-specific behaviors had to be handled, such as elements hidden in the DOM, fields requiring a double-click, and windows dependent on specific interactions.
userAutomation.solution4: The chosen approach prioritized implementation feasibility within the available timeframe.
userAutomation.decisionContext: The decision took into account the available timeframe and the requirements of the task.
userAutomation.decisionUsedText: It enabled registration automation through the system's existing workflow, without depending on the prior implementation of a new integration.
userAutomation.decisionAlternativeText: An API integration could offer greater robustness for a permanent solution, but would require additional development and validation.
userAutomation.role1: I carried out the technical analysis, defined the approach, and developed the automation in Python and Playwright.
userAutomation.role2: My responsibilities included understanding the registration workflow in TOTVS Protheus, identifying the elements required for automated interaction, handling WebApp-specific behaviors, and structuring input data reading.
userAutomation.role3: During execution, operational adjustments were also needed to handle inconsistencies in the received records, allowing registration of the intended users to be completed.
userAutomation.role4: The initiative demonstrated my ability to use programming to address a critical business need, balancing time constraints, technical complexity, and operational requirements.
userAutomation.results1: The automation enabled registration of approximately 140 users in TOTVS Protheus, meeting the operational need to integrate six new business units.
userAutomation.results2: One of the main challenges encountered during execution was input data quality.
userAutomation.results3: The CSV file, prepared by third parties based on previously supplied registration information, contained duplicate records that required manual intervention.
userAutomation.results4: When a duplicate was identified, processing had to be stopped so the file could be corrected and already processed records removed, allowing the automation to restart without repeating completed registrations.
userAutomation.results5: Despite these limitations, all intended users were registered.
userAutomation.results6: The experience highlighted opportunities for improvement, particularly preventive data validation, duplicate record detection, progress tracking, and safe resumption after interruptions.
userAutomation.opportunitiesNote: These improvements are identified opportunities, not features already implemented.

userAutomation.flow4: Registration based on a template user
userAutomation.flowExceptionText: Processing stops, the CSV is corrected manually, already processed records are removed from the list, and the automation is restarted manually.
userAutomation.flowNote: Duplicate handling and restarting the automation were manual.

erpSupport.title: ERP Support and Stabilization
erpSupport.pageTitle: ERP Support and Stabilization | Fernando Silva
erpSupport.description: Analysis and resolution of master data inconsistencies in TOTVS Protheus during the expansion of five business units, supporting tax document processing and operational continuity.
erpSupport.overview1: During the expansion into five new business units, TOTVS Protheus ERP application support and stabilization activities were needed, focusing on master data integrity and the continuity of business processes.
erpSupport.overview2: The work involved investigating and resolving inconsistencies in essential master data, supporting the processing of tax documents related to the transfer of acquired stock.
erpSupport.challenge1: The expansion involved importing customer, product, and product group master data.
erpSupport.challenge2: During stabilization, inconsistencies were identified in these records, including duplicate customers based on CNPJ (Brazilian corporate tax ID), duplicate products, and discrepancies in product group organization.
erpSupport.challenge3: These issues affected the processing of stock transfer invoices and required technical investigation and data cleansing.
erpSupport.challenge4: Operational criticality required prioritizing issues that hindered or prevented tax document processing.
erpSupport.solution1: The work relied on SQL Server and existing TOTVS Protheus features.
erpSupport.activity3: Identification of inconsistencies in customer, product, and product group records.
erpSupport.activity4: Support for master data cleansing in the ERP.
erpSupport.activity5: Review of issues affecting tax document processing.
erpSupport.solution2: No new customizations were developed for this work.
erpSupport.role1: I provided technical support for TOTVS Protheus during the expansion into five new business units, focusing on investigating master data inconsistencies and helping stabilize operational processes.
erpSupport.role2: Using SQL Server and existing ERP resources, I analyzed duplicate records and inconsistencies in customer, product, and product group master data, contributing to their resolution.
erpSupport.role3: The work was carried out in direct collaboration with the Tax team, using impact-based prioritization and focusing on issues that prevented or hindered the processing of stock transfer invoices.
erpSupport.role4: This work supported the continuity of material receipt processes and the operational stabilization of the new business units.
erpSupport.flowLabel: Steps in ERP application support and stabilization
erpSupport.flowNote: An investigation and resolution process carried out in collaboration with the Tax team.
erpSupport.flow3: Technical analysis with SQL Server and TOTVS Protheus
erpSupport.flow4: Joint prioritization with the Tax team
erpSupport.flow6: Support for processing stock transfer invoices
erpSupport.results1: The technical and functional work helped enable the processing of more than 15 stock transfer invoices, most containing approximately 250 items, during the expansion into five new business units.
erpSupport.results2: The work supported the cleansing of master data required for stock movements and the continuity of operational processes.
erpSupport.results3: The experience demonstrated the importance of ERP application support during expansion, particularly when data consistency and collaboration between Systems and Tax teams are essential to business operations.
erpSupport.itemsLabel: Items per invoice, in most documents
erpSupport.skill8: Collaboration between Systems and Tax teams.

sourceInventory.title: Protheus Source Code Inventory and Governance
sourceInventory.pageTitle: Protheus Source Code Inventory and Governance | Fernando Silva
sourceInventory.description: Development of tools to inventory ADVPL/TLPP source files and compare them with compiled objects in the Protheus RPO, identifying discrepancies and supporting ERP technical governance.
sourceInventory.overview1: In ERP environments with a history of customizations, maintaining traceability between compiled objects and their corresponding source files is an important challenge for system support and evolution.
sourceInventory.overview2: The project arose from the need to map the objects in the TOTVS Protheus RPO repository and compare them with the available ADVPL/TLPP files, identifying discrepancies and outstanding organizational tasks.
sourceInventory.challenge1: The presence of compiled objects in the ERP repository does not, on its own, guarantee that their corresponding source files are available and correctly identified.
sourceInventory.challenge2: An inventory was needed to provide visibility into the objects in the RPO, relate them to available files, and identify differences requiring analysis.
sourceInventory.challenge3: The goal was to improve visibility into legacy code and establish a reliable foundation for source file organization and version control initiatives.
sourceInventory.solution1: A Python solution was developed to create a technical inventory of source files and compare them with information extracted from the TOTVS Protheus RPO repository.
sourceInventory.activity2: Processing of information extracted from the RPO.
sourceInventory.activity6: Identification of outstanding source file organization tasks.
sourceInventory.solution2: The process was completed in full, providing a structured foundation for file organization and governance initiatives in the development environment.
sourceInventory.solutionNote: The project uses inventories and compiled object metadata; it does not recover or decompile original source code from the RPO.
sourceInventory.role1: I performed the technical analysis, defined the comparison criteria, and developed the tools used to collect, process, and organize the inventories.
sourceInventory.role2: The work involved investigating the available resources for identifying compiled objects in the RPO, developing the Python solution, and analyzing the generated results.
sourceInventory.role3: The initiative focused on improving visibility into software assets, supporting customization maintenance, and providing a technical foundation for the evolution of source code governance.
sourceInventory.flow4: Foundation for source code organization and governance
sourceInventory.flowNote: The comparison uses extracted data and the source file inventory; Python does not read the RPO directly.
sourceInventory.results1: The inventory and comparison of compiled objects in the RPO against available source files were completed in full.
sourceInventory.results2: The solution was run in the VS Code development environment, identifying matches, discrepancies, and outstanding organizational tasks.
sourceInventory.results3: The generated reports provided greater visibility into software assets and established a technical foundation for subsequent standardization and version control initiatives.
sourceInventory.limitations1: Although the solution fully met its functional objective, it was not packaged as a standalone executable.
sourceInventory.limitations2: Execution remained tied to the Python development environment in VS Code.
sourceInventory.limitations3: A future improvement could provide a standalone version, making the tool easier to use without running it directly from the development environment.
sourceInventory.skill1: Technical analysis of TOTVS Protheus and its RPO repository.

versionControl.title: Protheus Source Code Version Control Standardization
versionControl.pageTitle: Protheus Source Code Version Control Standardization | Fernando Silva
versionControl.description: Implementation of Git and GitHub version control practices to organize ADVPL/TLPP source code, standardize development workflows, and improve change traceability.
versionControl.overview1: A project to implement and standardize version control for TOTVS Protheus ERP ADVPL/TLPP source files, using Git and GitHub to organize development and provide traceability.
versionControl.overview2: The initiative aimed to improve source code management by replacing reliance on directories and manual copies with a version-controlled repository, change history, and documented usage practices.
versionControl.challenge1: The development environment had a history of customizations and files organized in directories, separating source files prepared for compilation from files under development.
versionControl.challenge2: This model made it difficult to trace changes, identify versions, and organize concurrent activities.
versionControl.challenge3: A structure was needed to centralize source files, preserve change history, and define consistent procedures for technical work.
versionControl.solution1: A Git/GitHub repository was implemented to manage Protheus source code, building on the information gathering and organization completed in the earlier RPO inventory project.
versionControl.activity3: Organization of classified files and files awaiting classification.
versionControl.activity7: Practical use of branches, commits, synchronization, and change integration.
versionControl.solution2: Guidance materials were prepared, including CONTRIBUTING.md documentation and operational instructions for using the workflow.
versionControl.solution3: Version control was put into use in real Protheus development and maintenance activities.
versionControl.role1: I analyzed the existing structure, planned the approach, and implemented the version control process for Protheus source code.
versionControl.role2: My involvement included initial repository organization, Git/GitHub environment setup, establishing usage conventions, and preparing technical documentation to guide the work.
versionControl.role3: I also used the version control workflow in real development activities, creating and updating branches, making commits, synchronizing with the remote repository, and integrating changes.
versionControl.role4: The initiative demonstrated my contribution to improving technical processes, organizing software assets, and adopting development governance practices.
versionControl.flowLabel: Steps in the version control process
versionControl.flowNote: The Git/GitHub working process, from source code inventory to change history and traceability.
versionControl.flow7: Integration of changes into the main repository
versionControl.results1: The project delivered a version-controlled repository for ADVPL/TLPP source code, with a structured organization and change history.
versionControl.results2: Documented Git/GitHub practices were established, including commit conventions and branch workflow procedures.
versionControl.results3: Version control was used in real ERP development and maintenance activities, with commits, synchronization with the remote repository, and change integration.
versionControl.results4: The initiative improved the foundations for source code traceability, organization, and control, establishing a technical basis for the evolution of governance practices.
versionControl.limitations1: Although the repository and version control practices were implemented, full adoption of the standardized workflow by all team members has not been confirmed.
versionControl.limitations2: Broader adoption, improved code reviews, and formal approval criteria represent opportunities for improvement.
versionControl.limitations3: The corporate presentation prepared for the project was not published.
versionControl.skill1: Git and GitHub applied to corporate development.
